pageCache.pageTitle: Westbridge awarded UNICEF RRS Silver Award - News - Westbridge Academy
pageCache.text:
Westbridge awarded UNICEF RRS Silver Award
We are delighted to announce that our school has achieved the Silver Rights Respecting School Award. This recognises our strong commitment to promoting children’s rights and embedding the values of respect, equality and inclusion across our school community. Achieving Silver means that children’s rights are well understood by pupils and staff and are actively influencing learning, behaviour and decision‑making throughout the school.
The assessor reflected that: It is clear that a child rights approach is increasingly being embedded at Westbridge Academy, with pupils learning about rights through assemblies, across the curriculum and through regular quiz activities designed to develop their rights fluency. Pupils described how “we learn about rights in our classrooms, from posters around the school, in our weekly assemblies and in the early morning work.” Senior leaders spoke of rights being “really ingrained across the entire school culture”, and staff described the links between school processes and rights, with the RRSA Coordinator explaining that “our behaviour system is based on the right to be heard.” Pupil leadership structures, including the People Parliament and class ambassadors, were referenced as contributing to the promotion of rights, with pupils leading assemblies and aspects of the quiz programme. Students were also able to outline specific changes they had made as a result of their leadership structures. A teacher noted that “there is a real sense of responsibility here… they are really empowered to make change.” Pupils also spoke positively about inclusion, sharing that “every culture, background, religion belongs here… we are all included. It is like a family.”
We are incredibly proud of our pupils and staff for their dedication and look forward to continuing our journey as a Rights Respecting School.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Executive Head Teacher
On behalf of the children and staff, it is with pleasure that I welcome you to Westbridge Academy. We are extremely proud of the strong values, educational achievements and the opportunities our children receive throughout their educational journey.
We place learners at the heart of everything and through our rich and ambitious curriculum, children learn in a safe and stimulating environment.
We pride ourselves in supporting all children to become life-long learners and successful adults in the modern World because of the strong foundations built from the moment children enter into our Academy.
Westbridge Academy values our diverse community and is committed to ensuring equity and inclusion for all children.
Our strong partnerships with other excellent academies in STEP, enables us to work together to strive for excellence.
As you navigate through our website, you will see passionate, confident and independent learners. We look forward to meeting you and showing you around our Academy so please book a visit.

pageCache.text:
Welcome from the Head Teacher
Welcome to Westbridge Academy at the heart of Battersea, where children are polite, kind and work hard in order to be successful. Westbridge is a beautifully-picturesque primary school hidden just a stone’s throw away from the River Thames with the vibrant Battersea Park a mere ten-minute stroll away.
Please explore our school website to discover our values and key information that provides a glimpse into our family-friendly school community.
We are a multi-cultural school that prides itself on both academic excellence and strong personal development of the whole child. Westbridge is diverse, nurturing and an inclusive school that constantly strives to provide every child with the very best opportunities during their time here in order to be successful in later life.
We work collaboratively with families and the wider community to ensure that our children are taught the skills they need to become successful, life-long learners as well as global citizens of the world.
We understand that children are the future of our community; therefore, children are at the heart of every decision we make, and we have an ambitious curriculum that reflects our diversity. We are strongly committed to anti-racism and equality as these elements guide everything that we do. We know that we must support and develop a child’s sense of self, so they can make knowledge-informed decisions about their future as they develop to become ready for secondary school and the wider world.
If you would like further information about what we can offer your child or have any questions or queries, please do not hesitate to contact the school to meet.

Art & DT
In these two highly creative areas of the curriculum, children are given the opportunity to learn skills which build on what has been taught before, so they can become confident designers and artists. In all learning, pupils are encouraged to make mistakes and learn from them, to evaluate their work and to make suggestions as to how things may be improved. In Art, pupils always have a focus on a particular artistic element and medium, as well as a particular artist as a stimulus for their work. In Design and Technology (DT), pupils develop their skills using a variety of media in order to design and make products for a particular audience or reason.

Our R.E. curriculum allows children to discover and gain an insight into the six religions within the world that we live by exploring important texts, festivals and beliefs. As with the rest of the curriculum, this knowledge is built upon and expanded as they progress through the school.

Music
At Westbridge Academy, our intention is that children develop an enthusiastic passion for music based on listening, singing, performing and discussing a wide range of musical styles, historical periods, and traditions. Our goal at Westbridge Academy is to create a catalyst for what will be a life-long love of music, full of curiosity and respectfulness. We are committed to ensuring children have the skills, knowledge, and confidence, to access, create, and enjoy all types of music that they may have the pleasure of experiencing throughout their lives.

Physical Education
At Westbridge Academy, we recognise the value of Physical Education (PE) and its importance in leading a healthier lifestyle as well as impacting cognitive skills, attitudes and academic behaviour. These include enhanced concentration and attention as well as improved classroom behaviour. It is important that children at Westbridge learn how physical activity benefits the body and how exercise encourages healthy lifestyles into adulthood.
PE at Westbridge encourages children to develop their fundamental movement skills such as running, jumping and throwing as well as providing opportunity to collaborate and work collaboratively as part of a team during matches.

Reception
In Reception, children learn through exploring and being active, as much of the learning in the EYFS is child-initiated. Westbridge Academy follows the national Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Framework, which has 7 main areas of development.
These prime areas are those most essential for your child’s healthy development and future learning. As children grow, the prime areas will help them to develop skills in four furthers Specific Areas.
Teachers carefully plan activities to suit the needs of individual learners. At Westbridge, children have access to a range of activities, both inside and outside the classroom, that support their progress through the Early Learning Goals.
Our pupils in Reception are given a firm foundation to begin the next stage of their education in Year 1.

English
EYFS (Nursery & Reception):
In Early Years (EYFS) and Year 1, we implement Fisher Family Trust’s (FFT) Success for All Phonics (SFA) programme to establish a strong foundation in early reading. This systematic synthetic phonics programme, validated by the DfE, provides a structured approach to phonics and early reading, focusing on phoneme-grapheme correspondences (GPCs), blending, and segmenting, which are essential for reading fluency.
In Reception, we introduce children to phonics through a phased, multisensory (actions, learning labs) approach that aligns with FFT’s principles. The programme begins with developing phonological awareness through activities involving sound discrimination, rhyme, and alliteration. By Term 1, pupils start learning short sound Phase 2 GPCs, allowing them to read simple CVC words. These lessons are designed to be engaging and active, involving actions, chants, and cooperative learning techniques to support memory and engagement.
In Year 1, the SFA Phonics programme continues to build on the foundation established in Reception. The focus shifts to more complex GPCs, including long vowel sounds, digraphs, and split digraphs, allowing pupils to decode multisyllabic words and recognize a wider range of Common Exception Words (CEWs).
Year 2 & Key Stage 2
By KS2, pupils have typically developed foundational decoding and phonetic skills, so our focus shifts towards reading fluency, comprehension, and critical thinking. We transition to a 6-day cycle in which reading and writing alternate, allowing for intensive, targeted practice in both areas. KS2 whole-class reading lessons are structured to support fluency, vocabulary expansion, and comprehension through diverse, age-appropriate texts that gradually increase in complexity.
At Westbridge, our writing curriculum encompasses two primary aspects: teaching writing within English lessons and discrete Grammar, Punctuation, and Spelling (GPS) lessons, as well as applied writing within the broader curriculum. In English lessons, children focus on a book and then write about a theme or topic related to it, covering a variety of genres to expose them to different types of writing. Early Years and Key Stage 1 (KS1) students write daily, while Key Stage 2 (KS2) students alternate between reading and writing over a 6-day cycle – 3 days reading followed by 3 days of writing.
Termly applied writing lessons allow children to apply the writing skills they have learned, demonstrating their understanding within their wider curriculum learning. This approach provides opportunities for children to apply their learning throughout the half term.
Our English programme is designed to expose children to a range of genres and texts, ensuring constant development in reading and writing skills. In KS1 and KS2, strategic assessments in both reading and writing help teachers select texts that meet the needs of all students, addressing gaps related to gender, Special Educational Needs and Disabilities (SEND), or Pupil Premium Grant (PPG) while providing additional support to ensure success.

History
At Westbridge Academy, we aim to help our pupils gain a coherent knowledge and understanding of Britain’s past and that of the wider world. We intend to inspire our pupils’ curiosity to know more about the past and equip them to ask perceptive questions, think critically, weigh evidence, sift arguments, and develop perspective and judgement. Pupils will reflect on how the past has shaped the world in which they live today.

Maths
Mathematics at Westbridge
At Westbridge, we want every child to develop a deep and lasting understanding of mathematics. Our curriculum is carefully sequenced so that learning builds step by step, enabling pupils to feel confident and secure in their knowledge rather than relying on rote procedures.
We structure learning through:
Collaborative learning is central to our approach. Pupils are encouraged to share, discuss and challenge ideas with one another, which strengthens reasoning and deepens understanding. This reflects our values of Passion, Urgency, Positivity, Aspiration and Commitment (PUPAC). We believe there is a difference between not knowing and not knowing yet — every child at Westbridge is supported to approach challenges with curiosity, resilience and ambition.

Nursery
At Westbridge, we have a 26-place Nursery which gives children a safe, creative space in which to learn and develop. If your child is 3 years old, and you are successful in your application to the Nursery, then they are entitled to 15 hours of free learning within the Nursery every week.
Sessions are divided into morning sessions (8:55 – 11:55am) and afternoon sessions (12:15 – 3:15pm), and your child will be allocated a place in either the morning or afternoon Nursery.
In our Nursery, we aim to apply the best principles of early years education, encouraging positive attitudes to school and its routines. Children have access to a range of activities, both inside and outside the classroom, and a variety of adult-led and child-led activities are on offer.
These Prime Areas are the most essential for your child’s healthy development and future learning.
You can download our Nursery application form, or come and see us in the Office to pick up a form.
